subject: Delta POC: SLO & failover qualification playbook
messages:
From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@delta.com>
Cc: camila_reyes <camila@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Delta POC: SLO & failover qualification playbook

Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed playbook for the Delta POC focused on reliability / SLO validation and hyperscaler comparison:

Summary from discovery:
- Goal: validate that Redwood’s serving runtime meets Delta’s operational SLOs and failover expectations under production-like load, and compare behavior to HyperscalerX.
- Focus areas: uptime under sustained traffic, rate limit behavior and throttling, failover time & error-budget burn characteristics, and regional/replica fallback.

Attached: delta-poc-slo-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook) and interop-test-plan.xlsx (test harness).

Proposed playbook (high-level):
1) Baseline: 1h warm-run at nominal QPS to capture steady-state latency/p99 and error rate.
2) Rate ramp: 30m step-up to 1.5x expected peak to observe throttling profiles and 429 patterns.
3) Failover sim: induce an out-of-region outage (target EU region) and measure failover transition time and p95/p99 delta.
4) Soak: 6h soak at 0.9x peak to evaluate error-budget depletion and GC/retry patterns.
5) Regression vs HyperscalerX: run identical traffic shape against HyperscalerX endpoint and collect token-level cost, p50/p95/p99, and error types.

Questions / asks for Delta team:
- Confirm do you want Redwood to run the simulated region outage or will Delta trigger it from infra?
- Can infra provide an account/API key and a test namespace by Aug 10?
- Any specific SLO targets beyond 99.9% uptime (e.g., p99 latency thresholds)?

Suggested window: Aug 10–12 for the initial validation. Ben will own test orchestration; Camila will coordinate scheduling/CS touchpoints.

Next: please review the attached playbook and reply with any edits, and confirm the infra contact (cc-ing infra@delta.com if helpful).

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Green <alex.green@delta.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Delta Infra Team <infra@delta.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta POC: SLO & failover qualification playbook

Aditya —

Appreciate the summary. Deck looks good at a glance. A couple things I want to clarify before we lock windows: 

1) Rate limits: our security policy prefers external endpoints to fail with 429s rather than silently queue—can Redwood simulate both behavior modes (aggressive 429 vs burst-throttle)?
2) Failover: we expect failover to a regional replica (EU fallback) with minimal session loss — can you outline how session affinity / KV cache warm-up will be handled?
3) HyperscalerX comparison: we'll need the same prompt corpus and a shared anonymized input set; can you produce a sampling script?

I'll loop infra and confirm if they will trigger the region outage. If they'd rather we ask Redwood to run the simulation, let us know the exact steps you will take.

Alex Green
Head of Platform Engineering
Delta Systems
From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@delta.com>
Cc: camila_reyes <camila@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta POC: SLO & failover qualification playbook

Alex —

Thanks — answers inline and a tighter checklist below. Attaching the playbook v1 for reference (delta-poc-slo-playbook-v1.pdf).

On rate limits: Redwood supports configurable throttling policies. For the POC we can run two modes back-to-back:
- Mode A: conservative (return 429 rapidly on quota exceed)
- Mode B: soft-throttle (queue / graceful degradation with gradual 5xx conversion)
We will instrument both and provide per-token metrics and 429/5xx counts.

On KV / session affinity and failover:
- We will exercise both sticky and stateless routes. For sticky routes we’ll show expected cache-warmup curves; for stateless fallback we’ll validate end-to-end correctness under KV miss.
- Expected failover transition time: target measurement is to capture the time from first failed connection to routing stabilization. In our experience, warm fallback takes ~2–8s depending on concurrency and model size; cold fallback (cold start) can be longer — we will record both.

On HyperscalerX comparison: we will provide a small sampling script and a sanitized input bundle. We'll ensure tokenization parity and record per-message token counts so results are comparable.

Tight checklist (owners and asks):
- Test account + namespace (Delta) — ACTION: Alex / infra to provide by Aug 6
- Test orchestration & traffic harness — OWNER: ben_carter — will deliver runbook and config by Aug 7
- Kernel / fallback validation & probe scripts — OWNER: priyom_das — will prepare instrumentation and expected threshold table (see below)
- CS coordination / logistics — OWNER: camila_reyes

Key thresholds we plan to verify (examples we’ll capture):
- Uptime: target >= 99.9% during soak; report windowed uptime and SLO burn rate
- p99 latency: target < 200ms for 256-token prompts under nominal load; we’ll show p50/p95/p99 curves
- Failover stabilization: target < 10s to route to warm replica; goal for warm fallback < 5s (best effort)
- Rate-limit behavior: compare 429 ratios and retry patterns between modes; measure error-budget consumption over the soak

If Delta would prefer Redwood to trigger the regional outage, we will provide a runbook and coordinate a maintenance window; otherwise have infra trigger it and drop a short confirmation into this thread.

Proposed schedule:
- Aug 6: provide test credentials and confirm namespace
- Aug 7: Redwood completes orchestration artifacts and runbooks
- Aug 10–12: execute POC runs (baseline, ramp, failover, soak, hypX comparison)

Next step: Alex, can you confirm the infra contact (if different than infra@delta.com) and sign off on the Aug 10–12 window? We'll lock Ben & Priyom's time.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, camila_reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta POC: SLO & failover qualification playbook

Adding a few technical notes for the team before runs:

1) Test account scope: we need an API key with the following scopes: generate:read, metrics:write, test-namespace:use. Please avoid production keys.
2) Models: recommend running the following variants to capture behavior across model sizes: small-quant (fast), base-fp16 (baseline), large-fp16 (stress).
3) Traffic generator config (attach interop-test-plan.xlsx):
   - Session length distribution: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 25% medium (64–256), 5% long (256–1024)
   - Concurrency profile: step-up every 5m; hold 15m at each step for sampling
4) Expected thresholds for initial pass (will be measured, not gated):
   - p50 < 50ms (small models), p95 < 120ms (base), p99 < 220ms (large) at nominal load
   - Failover routing stabilization < 8s measured as time for 95% of active requests to be handled by fallback pool
   - Rate-limit response onset: expect 429s to start appearing at ~1.25–1.5x provisioned QPS depending on route config

5) Logging & observability: Redwood will provide token-level latency breakdowns, per-route error types, and a short tracer for failover handoff time. Send a Drive link where collected artifacts should land.

I’ll upload the interop-test-plan.xlsx to the shared Drive after this note and finalize the traffic generator templates. Ben — once you have the runbook, ping me and I’ll add the probes.

—Priyom
Senior Applied ML / Inference
Redwood Inference
